title: CLTR Cutover shared reference definitions
description: Reference-tuple definitions (CLTR-CUTOVER-EXECUTABLE-SCHEMAS-001 v1.0 Sec.12, Sec.14). A valid reference proves shape only: it never implies the referenced record exists, is current, is authoritative, or that publication succeeded (Sec.40). The embedded cas_expectation component (row 10 of Sec.4, Sec.24) is added in Phase 136N (Implementation Group 4), the first group to need it (resolving DEFERRED-136H-1): it is embedded at exactly two sites in this phase, cutover_candidate.schema.json and certification.schema.json (both Sec.22/Sec.23 field tables carry a cas_expectation field), disclosed as NON-BLOCKING-136N-1 against Sec.4's own row-10 text naming cutover_candidate/publication_attempt as the two sites -- Sec.23's field table independently and unambiguously also lists cas_expectation on certification, so this phase follows the more specific per-family field tables over Sec.4's summary row, consistent with prior groups' precedent of favoring specific per-family tables over summary text (e.g. 136L's NON-BLOCKING-136L-2). A third embedding site, publication_attempt.schema.json, remains out of this phase's Group 4 boundary and is deferred to Group 5 (136P).

record_id.description: Always present. The referenced record's own record_id.

record_digest.description: Always present. The referenced record's own record_digest, shape-checked only.

record_family.description: Always present. Closed family tag preventing one family's record from silently masquerading as another (CSCH-EXEC-REQ-030).

schema_id.description: Conditionally present: required only where a reference crosses a family boundary whose schema-version compatibility is not otherwise implied by context. Optional where the reference is always to the same family and version as the referencing document.

schema_version.description: Conditionally present, alongside schema_id, for the same cross-family reason.

record_reference.description: Stable id+digest+family reference tuple. Does not verify the referenced record actually exists or matches the claimed family (Layer 4).

migration_epoch.description: Always present. Opaque migration-epoch token this reference is bound to.

epoch_digest.description: Conditionally present: an optional digest binding to a specific authority-epoch record's content, when the referencing family needs that stronger binding. A valid reference never implies the named epoch exists or is active -- that is an authority-resolver (Layer 6) responsibility, not implemented by this shared core.

epoch_reference.description: A shared reference shape used to bind a companion record to a migration epoch and, optionally, a specific authority-epoch record's digest. This is a reference shape only; it does not define, and this phase does not implement, an AuthorityEpoch or AuthorityState record schema.

generation_id.description: Always present. Always paired with generation_digest -- no bare, unpaired generation ID field exists anywhere in this package.

generation_reference.description: Stable id+digest generation reference. A valid reference never implies the referenced generation is certified, authoritative, or that publication of it succeeded (Sec.40).

proof_reference.description: Opaque, non-secret proof/signature reference, reusing record_reference's exact shape rather than a new one -- a proof reference is never a raw signature blob or reusable credential, only a pointer to a proof artifact stored elsewhere. Shape alone cannot distinguish a genuinely opaque reference from an embedded secret; this remains a documentation/convention-level guarantee (Sec.44), not a schema-enforceable one.

expected_authority_kind.description: Always present (Sec.24). Every expected-state field in this $def is required -- missing values are never wildcards.

expected_authority_epoch.description: Always present (Sec.24). Family-tagged reference restricted to authority_epoch, preventing a wrong-family substitution.

expected_authoritative_generation.description: Always present (Sec.24). Sec.24's field table types this 'record_reference', but this package's existing precedent (authority_state.schema.json's authoritative_generation field, Phase 136J) types a generation binding as the dedicated id+digest-only generation_reference shape rather than the id+digest+family record_reference shape, since 'generation' is not itself one of the 16 record_family enum values (shared/enums.schema.json) and so cannot be family-restricted the way other record_reference fields are. Disclosed as NON-BLOCKING-136N-2: a documented, precedent-consistent typing choice, not an invented field.

expected_authority_pointer_digest.description: Always present (Sec.24). Shape-checked only; this package defines no authority pointer record and does not resolve or create one.

expected_authority_state_digest.description: Always present (Sec.24). The expected digest of an AuthorityState record's own content. Shape-checked only; never recomputed or compared against a live AuthorityState document at Layer 2.

expected_source_lifecycle_state.description: Always present (Sec.24). Restates, by wire value only, the 12-value legacy LifecycleState enum already implemented at src/pcae/cltr/enums.py (CLTR-SCHEMA-001) -- this package does not import that Python enum or depend on it; it independently re-declares the exact same closed vocabulary as plain JSON Schema string values. Unknown-value behavior: reject.

expected_request_reference.description: Always present (Sec.24). Family-tagged reference restricted to cutover_request.

expected_certification_reference.description: Always present (Sec.24). Family-tagged reference restricted to certification. When this $def is embedded inside certification.schema.json itself (Sec.23), a schema-valid document may structurally reference any certification record_id/digest, including in principle its own -- JSON Schema validates one document's shape only and cannot compare a nested reference's id/digest against its own envelope's record_id/record_digest (Layer 4). Disclosed as NON-BLOCKING-136N-3: self-reference exclusion for this embedding site is a semantic-validator responsibility, not a Layer 2 schema-shape responsibility.

cas_expectation.description: The embedded CASExpectation component (row 10 of Sec.4, Sec.24). Never a standalone document with its own record_id; created together with, and digested as part of, its owning document (cutover_candidate or certification, this phase; publication_attempt, a future Group 5 site). No optional fields -- every expected-state field is mandatory, which is precisely the mechanism preventing a missing value from being treated as an unbound wildcard (CLTR-CUTOVER-EXECUTABLE-SCHEMAS-001 v1.0 Sec.24, restated by the Phase 136 implementation plan Sec.13 Group 4 no-go criteria).
